positioning_incumbents: Existing cheap, white-box safety metrics fall into two groups, neither of which is a parent-free, leave-one-lineage-out, few-prompt, per-checkpoint screen validated against benchmark safety. The first needs a reference: \citet{Lee2026}'s Skin-Deep fragility score contrasts an aligned model against its own base checkpoint; \citet{Huang2026}'s RAS needs a per-family reference model plus a calibration set with other models' measured ASR, and states explicitly that raw scores are not cross-family comparable; \citet{Hurtado2026}'s two-signal audit reaches AUROC 0.95 and a genuine leave-one-family-out balanced accuracy of 0.89, but only by anchoring to a reference checkpoint per family, and only for a binary abliteration label. The second is parent-free but not predictive: \citet{Messenger2026}'s AMS holds out only its classification threshold (71\%, 10/14) while its headline behavioral correlation (r=-0.546, p=.043, n=14) is in-sample; \citet{Lin2026}'s N-GLARE needs 7000+ offline trajectories and reports rank-correlation robustness, not a cross-model headline; and \citet{Lan2026}'s HRCI is explicitly disclaimed by its own authors as "not a safety score." Cross-model regressions such as \citet{Li2026}'s per-model steering slope and \citet{Leong2025}'s template-region NIE are fit in-sample per model, with no held-out lineage.
